entry.title: blacklist
entry.content:
Blacklist
This is a sample blacklist that allows users to see what a blacklist is and how it functions. Blacklists allow users to readily keep track of those who they have blocked across protocols or set to Do-Not-Interact (DNI) within their circles. Blacklists can be employed by individual users, communities, wheelcores, landhubs, systems, federations, and any other kind of entity within Asveora. Some blacklists may be publicly shared for others to reference such as Asveora's network blacklist or kept private depending on the needs of the blacklist's author.

What you are reading right now is the blacklist's description where you can detail how the blacklist functions and its use cases. To make a blacklist private simply remove it from your library index, store it on a .html page that is not named 'blacklist' to avoid others being able to view it, and do not share a link to it. Blacklists are not just limited to entities within Asveora either. You can also add websites, organizations, or individuals and groups from other platforms to your blacklist as well.

entry.title: constitution
entry.content:
Table of Contents
00. Key Terms
01. Preamble
02. Age of Citizenship
03. Agreements & Obligations
04. Privacy & Security
05. Once Free Always Free
06. Data Ownership, DMCAs, & Protections
07. Human Rights Statement
08. Democratic Rights & Network Removals
09. Prohibition of Disruptive Organization
10. Appropriate Usernames
11. Accessing Matrix & Staying Safe
12. Transfer & Backup of Communications Profile
13. Liability Disclaimer
14. Content Sharing Expectations
15. Impersonation & Badges
16. Buying & Selling in the Services Marketplace
17. Advertisements, Paywalls, & External Marketplaces
18. Malicious Links, Malware, & Attacks
19. AI Generated Content
20. Agreement to the Constitution
21. History of the Constitution
Meanings of Terms
When we say "Asveora," "we," "us," and "our" in these terms, we mean Asveora LLC, asveora.social, and its related organizations.
When we say "services" in these terms, we mean Asveora's and asveora.social’s services, apps, websites, and other products.
When we say "user", "citizen", "member", and "Asveoran" in these terms, we mean users and members of Asveora's and asveora.social’s services, apps, websites, and other products.
When we say "you" or "your," we mean you. If you’re accessing our services on behalf of a legal entity (like your employer), you agree that you have the authority to bind that entity to these terms, and "you" and "your" will refer to that entity.
When we say "External Visitors" in these terms, we mean persons and entities that are not members of the asveora.social network but may be interacting with services, communities, or other creations created and operated by Asveorans.
I. The Preamble of Asveora
Asveora is a digital network that operates on the model of a Decentralized Democratic Constitutional Republic (DDCR) and serves with the purpose of helping people become more technologically self-sustainable and independent while also combatting the faults of centralized social media and Late Stage Web 2. It has been built with the intent to generate authentic connections and discussions while cutting out all of the white noise and pandemonium that has become so common elsewhere over the internet. This constitution that you are now reading is the official Terms of Service (ToS) of the Asveora network (also known as the asveora.social network). It applies to your access to and use of Asveora and any virtual properties directly related to it. This constitution was drafted by the first declared federation of Asveora known as “Asveora Genesis”. While this constitution is subject to amendment by the inalienable political power of the populace of Asveora, some guidelines, statutes, and directives cannot be amended if they exist to comply with national or international laws.
II. Age of Citizenship
To become a citizen of Asveora you must be at least 16 years of age and meet the minimum age of digital consent in your country. If your country’s minimum age of digital consent is under 16, the declared minimum age of Asveora will be honored. If your country’s minimum age of digital consent is over 16 then it will be honored instead. Depending on the protocols and guidelines of different federations, systems, landhubs, communities or wheelcores you may need to be older so be sure to read all additional terms and requirements when navigating Asveora. If you are old enough in your country to become a member of Asveora, but not old enough to have authority to consent to the terms provided in this constitution, your parent or guardian must agree to these terms on your behalf.

Please ask your parent or guardian to read these terms with you. If you are a parent or legal guardian, and you allow your adolescent to use Asveora, then these terms also apply to you, and you are completely responsible for your adolescent’s activity within Asveora. If you are accepting these terms and engaging with Asveora on behalf of a company, organization, or other legal entity, you represent and warrant that you are authorized to do so and have the authority to bind such entity to these terms, in which case the words “you” and “your” as used in these terms shall refer to such entity. In accordance with using Asveora, you understand and state that:

01. You are at least 16 years old and over the minimum age required by the laws of your country of residence to access and use Asveora.

02. You can form a binding contract with Asveora, or, if you are 16 or older but under the age of majority in your jurisdiction, that your legal guardian has reviewed and agrees to these terms.

03. No one under 16 is allowed to use or access Asveora. Federations, systems, landhubs, or wheelcores may require you to be older to access them so please read all additional terms and requirements when navigating Asveora’s online social network.

04. You are not barred from using Asveora under any and all applicable laws in your region.

05. You have not been blacklisted from Asveora.

06. If you are accepting these terms on behalf of another legal entity, you represent that you have full legal authority to bind such entity to these terms.

If you encounter anyone within Asveora who is under the age of 16 years, mandatory reporting is required. There are no exceptions. If you encounter someone whose age meets the minimum age requirement (16 years of age) but is not an adult (18 years of age or older) and they are attempting to access content or conversations restricted for an adult audience, it is your job prohibit them from doing so within the reasonable means of your own power. Especially if you yourself are an adult. No IFs, ANDs, or BUTs. You are the adult and they are the child. It is your responsibility to remind them that they are a child and that certain content and conversations are not suitable for them. Document the situation and report it if they (the child) are refusing to listen and begin harassing you (the adult) about the matter. Harassment of any kind is not tolerated within Asveora under section VII of the constitution. Be a good role model that others can trust and look up to. Help make our world a better and safer place. And if you are the parent or legal guardian of a network member, you are legally responsible for the well-being and safety of those who you have been tasked with guarding. Child endangerment is illegal and a very serious issue and any funny business or excuses will not be tolerated whatsoever.
III. Agreements & Obligations Within Asveora and Beyond
Asveora is an online social network that puts all of the choices and creative power in the hands of the user. This means that you will be accessing other services and tools in order to build the foundation of what will be your new digital home on the internet. You are expected to read and understand the terms and services of the following but not limited to: Your domain registrar, your matrix homeserver, your file hosting service, and any other entities that you engage with. In addition, every federation, system, landhub, community, and wheelcore has their own policies so make sure to read and understand those policies as you are bound to them if you engage with those entities. All federations, systems, landing hubs, and wheels agree to this constitution in being a part of Asveora.
IV. Privacy & Security
Asveora is committed to ensuring privacy and security through transparency and education. Asveora does not collect, use, nor share the information about you when you access or use its network and it severely discourages anyone attempting to do such. There is no long-winded privacy policy here to read but instead here are some crucial notes about security and safety in Asveora and strategies you can employ across the internet.

01. Create strong passwords for the means by which you will access Asveora. Use a strong mix of characters and symbols that will not be easily brute forced or guessable by malicious figures. The more complex and unique your password is, the better.

02. Do not share your passwords with anyone else aside from yourself and yourself alone.

03. Make sure that your passwords are stored securely inside of an encrypted file on your choice of digital hardware or service. Never store your passwords in your e-mail, a personal diary, or in other insecure locations.

04. Never give out your e-mail address, phone number, home address, and other sensitive information.

05. Read the terms and conditions of every tool and service that is external to Asveora. Read their policies to ensure that they are respecting your privacy and security in full.

06. Never enter your financial or personal information on a website that is not secure. Always look for “https://” and a padlock icon in your web browser’s address bar. And even then, you may be required to vet the website yourself to make sure that it is not a phishing pond disguised as a secure website.

07. Never click suspicious web links or shortened web links and do not accept cookies from websites that you are not familiar with. Always run shortened or sketchy web links through trusted link checking services or use the built in developer tools of your web browser to inspect the link for anything out of the ordinary.

08. Do not share your IP address, MAC address, or device ID with anyone.

09. If you suspect that your financial information has been stolen, immediately contact your bank.

10. If you suspect that your IP address has been leaked in some form, immediately obtain a new one.

11. Do not ever trust insecure public WiFi networks. Always make sure they are secured in some form.

12. Be conscious of and actively manage your personal data wherever you go.

13. Enable multi-factor authentication whenever it is available.

14. Use a reputable VPN service to keep your IP address safe and sound.

15. Never provide links to sources where your personal information may be visible. Always disclose the privacy and security policies of the links to materials and sites that you may share.

16. No one from Asveora will ever ask you for your e-mail address, phone number, home address, device serial number, IP address, MAC address, credit card, driver’s license, or any other form of personal or critical data. There are no official offices or employees of Asveora, so if anyone contacts you posing as an employee of Asveora and asks for sensitive information, immediately report them to the support and assistance channels of whatever wheelcore, landhub, system, and or federation that you are a part of. If anyone asks for your sensitive information or is devising ways to aggregate data of you and others within the network, be sure to report them as well. Asveora is dedicated to security, trust, and integrity.
V. Once Free Always Free
Asveora was made by the public for the public. You are not allowed to license, sell, transfer, assign, distribute, host, or use Asveora as a commercial exploit. If someone is telling you that you need to buy a license or sign up for a subscription to join Asveora, immediately take note and try to report it within Asveora. Asveora will always be free to join and participate within as the network is entirely made up of and run by its members. Invasive advertisements (such as pop-ups, interstitial ads, banner ads, etc.), micro-transaction schemes, dubious online marketplaces, and any unethical monetary exploits will not be tolerated anywhere within the network. The network is entirely financially supported by those of who it is composed.
VI. Data Ownership, DMCAs, and Protections
Your creations, your data, and the way in which you access Asveora is entirely placed under your control. No one owns your data, creations, or the ways in which you access Asveora except you and the services or tools you select to craft your experience. If you are having trouble with digital content theft of any kind, feel free to reach out to the wheelcore, landhub, system, and or federation that you are a part of. If you are a part of a wheelcore, landhub, system, or federation that does not serve you well, you are always free to either start your own or join a different one. If you are a part of asveora.social but feel it is not serving you well, you are also free to completely disconnect your presence from the network, start your own network, and move all of your data with you. Asveora has no legal right to your data nor your content and will never claim ownership of either at any point.

As such, this also means that Asveora is not responsible for the content or data that you choose to share as per Section 230 of USA law. The only user content that Asveora may host is any user-submitted content for indexing items such as landhubs, communities, and wheelcores. If Asveora receives a DMCA request for any the content of any indexed item, it will remove the infringing content in accordance with the takedown request. Please provide the following information and acknowledge the guidelines when submitting a DMCA request:
01. A physical or electronic signature of the person authorized to act on behalf of the copyright owner

02. Identification of where the original copyrighted work is located

03. Identification of where the infringing material is located on our website by providing a maximum of 10 URLs to a direct download and not an information page in the body of an email

04. The full name, mailing address, telephone number, and email address of the copyright owner or an authorized agent

05. A statement by the copyright owner or an authorized agent that upon a good faith belief, the disputed use of the material is not authorized by the copyright owner, its agent, or the law

06. A statement that under penalty of perjury, the information in the notice is accurate and you are the copyright owner or authorized to act on behalf of the copyright owner

07. A scanned physical document that proves you are the copyright owner or authorized to act on behalf of the copyright owner

08. A valid email address such as username@copyrightcompany and not one from free email services (Gmail, Hotmail, iCloud, etc.) to help prove you are the copyright owner or authorized to act on behalf of the copyright owner

09. An email in plain text (no rich text such as HTML) sent to support (dot) asveora (at) proton (dot) me, sending an email to our ISPs means your notice will not be processed

10. Access to content files, not information pages, may be restricted as only content files might or might not violate someone's copyright

11. Personal or attorney notices will not be processed, they must come from companies or dmca/eucd agents
VII. Human Rights Statement
Asveora stands for the mutual respect and care for all humans no matter their sex, gender, race, religion, geography, language, national origin, social origin, and other identifying characteristics. It does not and will not tolerate sexism, sexual harassment, racism, transphobia, xenophobia, homophobia, discriminatory language, discriminatory behavior, slurs, hate-speech, and other forms of hate, discrimination, harassment, or prejudice from any individual or entity towards another individual or entity for any reason. Always remember the human behind the screen.
VIII. Democratic Rights and Network Removals
Asveora is built upon the model of a Decentralized Democratic Constitutional Republic (DDCR). This means that the executive direction is determined through the political discourse and voting abilities of the members of Asveora whether it be in a wheelcore, landhub, system, or a federation. Asveorans have the right to vote on all polled issues within Asveora as this is a part of their democratic rights. External Visitors on the other hand cannot vote since they are not members / citizens of Asveora. No person or entity within Asveora can cast a vote on behalf of a person or entity outside of Asveora.

If an issue arises within Asveora such as ToS violations or other kinds of misbehavior, an Asveoran may file a complaint in the Stoat server of the Asveora Network Plaza community. Depending on the issue, they may also be recommended to report the issue to the platform provider or server host. Filing a complaint will trigger a court case. Every Asveoran has a right to due process and the proceedings for any administrative discipline will follow the outcome of a court case as these cases are held to determine the resolution to an issue.

Asveorans are required to report to the Asveora Network Plaza community’s Stoat server if they are summoned to Asveora’s court. Being summoned to the court (also known as a court summons) is a mandatory directive and the Asveoran that is being summoned must appear within the provided time frame declared by the court summon. This still applies even if they primarily reside on another platform and protocol different from Stoat. Asveorans that do not appear for their court summon will be FTA (Failure to Appear) and given a strict countdown period before their FTA status converts into automatic disciplinary action which may result in a network ban.

Court cases are held to ensure the fair treatment of every Asveoran and an honest assessment of the raised issue. They include the participation of every assembly within Asveora. Court case outcomes are determined by the review of a composite jury to ensure that rulings are truly democratic in execution. Depending on the severity of the violation, the case might be expedited at the direction of the Administrative and Executive assemblies to ensure network safety and security.

The governing matters of Asveora are not to be conflated nor confused with the legal systems of real world countries. For instance, if a user breaches their agreement to the constitution of Asveora but breaks no laws of their country or international laws, they may be removed from Asveora but may not be in real life legal trouble. If a user breaches their agreement to the constitution of Asveora which involves them breaking the laws of their country or international laws, they may be removed from Asveora and subsequently reported to the appropriate agencies.

The democratic right to vote may be revoked from an Asveoran if they are on trial within the network. Network removals are a highly unlikely occurrence as they are decided by network wide review. This is being noted here because if you are removed from Asveora, you might have more pressing problems on your hands to worry about than just being removed from the network. Just as with other administrative actions, network removals can be appealed, but the process may take a substantial amount of time. However you most likely will never have to worry about such happening if you follow the laws of your country and the constitution of Asveora. Network removals also does not mean you cannot deploy Asveora independently since the project is open source. It just means you will be removed from the asveora.social ecosystem and barred from participating.

External Visitors cannot be summoned under any circumstance since they do not exist as a member / citizen of the Asveora network. Therefore Asveora does not govern them in any direct manner. If an External Visitor violates the ToS of Asveora, they must be dealt with directly by the Asveoran that is operating the space where External Visitor access has been enabled. If an External Visitor violates the ToS of the instance or platform that they are using, then they must be reported to the appropriate departments of that instance or platform that have been tasked with handling trust and safety.
IX. Prohibition of Disruptive Organization
Asveorans may not engage in, promote, or create the following: Brigades, political gladiatorism, reaction bait boards, astroturfing, recruiting / raising internet armies, unsolicited services, shock content, flash mobs, using Asveora to incite unrest, using Asveora to declare war other entities (whether physical or virtual), planning of raids, extremist content, executing raids, spamming, swatting, doxxing (this includes the compilation of public information for malicious purposes), "ironic" meme communities, "ironic" groupthink boards, drama hubs, free-speech rooms, peanut gallery boards, and any other mechanism or structure that is created with the goal of bringing about extreme controversy, extreme distress, or antisocial behavior.
X. Appropriate Usernames
Usernames are expected to be appropriate and function primarily as a unique indentifier within Asveora. While you are free to customize your 12 character username string however you like, make sure that it does not contain offensive words and phrases. Any username that contains or references slurs, hate groups, tragic events, aggressive statements, and threatening language will be rejected and you will be asked to change your username during the registration process.
XI. Accessing Matrix and Staying Safe
You are prohibited from accessing the public Matrix ecosystem with your Asveora account. If you would like to access the public Matrix ecosystem then please create a separate Matrix account for that purpose. Matrix is an amazing protocol with a massive decentralized community of its own, but the protocol has been abused by bad actors due to its decentralized nature. To ensure your safety it is mandated that you only interact with members of Asveora and Asveoran communities on Matrix. Any unverified or external entities should be promptly reported and removed from spaces or rooms. When in doubt, always check the usernames database or consult the administration of Asveora.

Occasionally you may be contacted through direct messaging rooms by the host of a homeserver that you are using with information regarding updates about the status, security, and upgrades of a homeserver. You do not need to respond to these. If you end up having any problems with your Matrix account on a certain homeserver, directly email the host of the homeserver (their contact information can usually be found at the homeserver's root domain) rather than processing the issue directly through the Matrix protocol.

NEVER accept direct messaging room invites from accounts that you have not interacted with in a common setting somewhere within the Asveora network. If you are contacted with content that is prohibited under rule XIV then immediately report the account to the Asveora administration through a support channel on Stoat and flag the content for the host of the homeserver you're using by using the report function within your Matrix client.

No one from the Asveora administration will ever ask for your name, phone number, credit card, street address, ID, or any kind of identifying information. If someone reaches out asking for sensitive information or posing as a member of Asveora's administration then immediately report the behavior and block them. Always ask in a support channel if you are unsure or have concerns about an account that you have come across.
XII. Transfer and Backup of Communications Profile
In the case of the matrix protocol and similar chat protocols, Asveorans may transfer homeservers or create backup presences on other homeservers as long as they employ their verified APC (Asveora Profile Code) which will serve as the key for re-authentication when adding backup presences into the network or making transfers. Asveorans may not pair an APC with more than one APA (Asveora Profile Address) as it will may risk invalidating their AUID (Asveora User ID) or causing conflicts in the network’s logs. When a homeserver transfer is happening or a backup is being created, the Asveoran must show proof of authorship in the scanning process by adding the homeserver details to their profile space for the designated period of time as per given instruction.
XIII. Liability Disclaimer
Asveora is not liable for you nor is it responsible for your data or the data that you share. You are responsible for yourself, your data, and the data that you share at all times. If something is concerning you, never hesitate to speak up and seek out the proper assistance. While Asveora is not liable for you, the network is akin to a family as citizens are committed and expected to be committed to looking out for the health and safety of one another at all times.
XIV. Content Sharing Expectations
All Asveorans have the responsbility of being mindful about the content that they share within the Asveora network. Content promoting, soliciting, or encouraging hate speech, violent extremism, scams, illegal content, graphic shock material, and self-harm are completely prohibited. Profiles, communities, and landhubs containing adult content such as violence or sexually explicit material must deploy the age verification page in front of them. This is extremely crucial and taken very seriously.
XV. Impersonation & Badges
Impersonating individuals, organizations, companies, or entities that you do not represent is entirely prohibited. Do not create presences with the intention to deceive or confuse others about the legitimate identity of another individual or entity. This may also include copying the name or likeness of another to deceive others about the ownership or affiliation of a profile. Do not assign various operational or contributor badges to yourself if your are not contributing to the Asveora project. While you are free to assign whatever kinds of badges you want on your profile (after all that is the fun of Asveora) we ask that if you want to display a contributor badge for development, community support, bug hunting, or other operational activities then get involved! We always love having more hands on deck than less and there is plenty of work happening on Asveora at all hours of the day.
XVI. Buying & Selling in the Services Marketplace
All buyers, sellers, and other participants within the services marketplace of asveora.social must be members of the network. If you are not a member of the network you cannot purchase services, sell services, or participate in any kind of transaction involving Asveora’s services marketplace. This is to ensure that all transactions are properly logged within the network. All transactions utilizing Asveora’s services marketplace MUST be reported through the appropriate channel within the Stoat server of the Asveora Network Plaza community. If you decide to operate outside of Asveora’s services marketplace, Asveora is not responsible for any damages that may incur.

The asveora.social network and Asveora project do not make money from transactions, process transactions, or offer protections on transactions. Asveora will intervene with a network ban if fraud is discovered in order to ensure the integrity of its marketplace. However the marketplace strictly acts as a search engine and operates operates under Section 230 of USA law.

This means that it cannot be legally held liable for the offerings of a 3rd party. All sellers within the services marketplace are considered 3rd party entities and freelancers. They are not employed by Asveora or associated officially with the organization in any capacity. Asveora does not sell, offer for sale, or direct the sale of any services. It simply provides a search engine for independent parties who are offering services to the public (fellow Asveorans). If you come across a listing or seller that is encouraging the sale of fraudulent services, please immediately report it through the support center if you are not within the network. If you are within the network then please report it both through the support center and the support channel of the Asveora Network Plaza Stoat server.

Fraud is taken extremely seriously as it damages trust in the marketplace and hurts people. Fraud victims will be redirected to the proper legal resources if they wish to pursue legal action from within their territory. Asveora is not a legal agency nor legal advisor and is not authorized to offer any professional legal advice in any official capacity. Please use the proper sources you are redirected to. In order to be added to the Asveora’s marketplace listings as a service provider you must complete the appropriate verification process that is established within the network for becoming a listed seller. All listings are recommendations and, as previous outlined, sellers are not officially associated with Asveora in any legal capacity. All sellers are responsible for determining the payment processor they will use (PayPal, Stripe, Wise, Square, etc.) and how the taxes are handled from what they make through freelancing.

Asveora does not process taxes or offer tools to assist sellers with doing so. If a seller chooses to use an untrustworthy or controversial payment processor, their listings may be removed from the marketplace. Cryptocurrency and virtual items are not allowed as a transaction solution and any seller requesting for cryptocurrencies, NFTs, blockchain items, or virtual assets such as video game skins as a form of payment will be removed from the market. This is enforced to ensure transparency and safety.
XVII. Advertisements, Paywalls, & External Marketplaces
Advertisements within the Asveora network are only allowed if they are not invasive in nature as outlined in section V. They should not disrupt the user experience or obstruct content. No one likes getting bombarded by ads that completely lock up navigation or present themselves like they might give your device a dozen viruses. Advertisements and sponsorships must be disclosed as such in an explicit manner. Paywalls are entirely prohibited. You are free to encourage donations to support your work however. Links to external marketplaces are allowed but Asveora is not responsible for the products or services offered in those marketplaces and cannot be legally held liable for any damages incurred by using them. Asveora does not receive commissions, monetary gifts, or payouts from any of the external marketplaces that Asveorans may link to.
XVIII. Malicious Links, Malware, & Attacks
The sharing of malicious links, sharing of malware, or the execution of web or device attacks of any kind will result in a network removal. This includes, but not limited to, phishing, IP grabbers, fuzzing, ransomware, cryptojacking, man-in-the-middle attacks (MITM), cross-site scripting (XSS), cross-site request forgery (CSRF), SQL injection, and plenty of other malicious behaviors that seek to compromise the device, security, or identity of an individual, service, organization, or other entity.
XIX. AI Generated Content
The Asveora network (asveora.social) is committed to transparency, trust, and safety. AI generated content must be marked as such within the network. With an increasing volume of AI generated content circulating around on the internet as the months and years go on, Asveora wants to ensure that Asveorans know what content they are looking at and how that content came to be. No matter how you feel personally about AI, never attempt to pass off AI generated content as being generated or produced by other means. Honesty and integrity is highly valued within Asveora and we want to ensure that those values are carried through how media and content is shared.

AI generated content that is created to deceive, harm, or exploit individuals is entirely prohibited and will result in a ban from the network. This includes but is not limited to deepfakes, AI manufactured events, and AI editing processes that obscure the true contents or events of a piece of non-AI generated media. Parody creations utilizing technologies such as voice cloning may only be allowed if explicitly marked as being AI generated and a parody. These parodies must also not exist to harm, exploit, or deceive. If they do, the same penalties and restrictions outlined above will apply in full.
XX. Agreement to the Constitution
By accessing and or using Asveora, you agree to this constitution and the statements made within it. You will be bound by the terms presented and it is assumed that you have read this document with care and understand it in addition to the fact that you are responsible for keeping yourself informed of changes to the constitution. You understand and agree that you will be held accountable for any breach of this constitution. This constitution must be publicly displayed in every federation, system, landhub, and wheelcore.
XXI. History of the Constitution
2023-01-06: The constitution of Asveora is drafted by the first citizens of Asveora and the first declared federation of Asveora known as "Asveora Genesis" on January 6th, 2023. It is ratified that day at 9:00 PM (EST/UTC-5).
2023-04-07: The first amendments to the constitution of Asveora are made and signed into action on April 7th, 2023 at 3:00 AM (EDT/UTC-4).
2026-04-11: The second amendments to the constitution of Asveora are made and signed into action on April 11th, 2026 at 12:43 PM (EDT/UTC-4).
2026-04-19: The third amendments to the constitution of Asveora are made and signed into action on April 19th, 2026 at 9:33 PM (EDT/UTC-4).

Framework Versions
This is a complete directory of the Asveora framework's various versions. While some quality of life features may be added into older versions of Asveora to match operational standards, they will largely remain the same as when they were originally published. This is to ensure that Asveorans and anyone else using the Asveora framework have the freedom to choose which version of Asveora they prefer to deploy. Please keep in mind that some versions of Asveora might have shared features depending on the introduction of certain components and only the distinct elements of each version are separated for deployment. For example, v3 and v4 have completely different profile space layouts but otherwise share all of the same features with v4 having more features than v3. To find the latest releases, please visit Asveora's GitHub page where all repositories related to Asveora are maintained and archived.
